The significance lies less in the amount than in who carries the risk.
Before the award, iX held SGD0.9m of cash in
FY25 and would likely have needed repeated dilutive raises to fund a Phase 3 programme of this scale.
The programme is now externally funded, and iX retains the commercial rights.
The contract also flows through the income statement. FY26 revenue included SGD1.2m of development services linked to the programme. The contract should likely give revenue visibility over the next two years.
•
EUA offers an early proof-point ahead of Phase 3
– The US Secretary of War's military emergency determination on 15 Jul 2026 and the declaration by the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) on 31 Aug 2026 (published on 3 Sep 2026) created the legal pathway for FDA to consider emergency use of drugs for moderate-to-severe acute pain in military casualties.
Wafermine is not named, but it is the programme DoD is funding, and iX could potentially complete its EUA filing in 4Q26, with approval potentially in 1Q27 and initial DoD supply potentially from 2Q27.
Before Phase 3 data, an EUA would show that FDA accepts the chemistry, manufacturing and controls (CMC) package, that iX can manufacture at commercial scale in the US and that DoD demand is real.
The direct financial contribution is likely to be modest at first. Management indicates potential EUA supply of about USD6.6–13.2m over the three-year contract. However, we think EUA approval would strengthen confidence in the platform and in Wafermine's path to full approval.
•
Phase 3 design risk is likely low, with commercial value tied to label and partner
– Wafermine's Phase 2b study in 125 post-surgical patients delivered a pooled effect size of 0.65 at the 75mg dose (p<0.01) across bunionectomy and abdominoplasty models, and the Phase 3 programme is expected to use the same models and primary endpoint, with studies potentially starting in 3Q27 and topline data potentially in 2Q28.
Repeating a successful design reduces protocol risk, and the Jan 2025 FDA approval of Vertex's Journavx (suzetrigine), whose pivotal trials used the same two surgical models, sets a recent precedent for a non-opioid on this endpoint.
Beyond approval, commercial value depends on how Wafermine is positioned.
Racemic ketamine is generic, a US Schedule III controlled substance, and its dissociative effects could invite prescribing restrictions in outpatient settings.
A favourable label and a well-capitalised partner would therefore be key to unlocking Wafermine's full value.

iX is consolidating its compounding assets and nutraceuticals into Ligo Pharma, under a partnership framework with GLD Partners, LP and its wholly owned subsidiary Orion Specialty Labs, an FDA-registered 503B outsourcing facility in Nevada.
Eddy Lee, Chairman and CEO, iX Biopharma.
The 503B route does allow sales to hospitals, clinics and 503A pharmacies without new clinical trials, and a pharmaceutical-grade freeze-dried wafer is differentiated in a segment dominated by basic reformulation.
However, a 503B facility may compound from a bulk drug substance only where FDA has listed that substance for clinical need or the drug is in shortage, and FDA's ongoing review of which peptides may be compounded shows the perimeter is still being redrawn.
We therefore take a measured approach, assuming a subset of the pipeline launches at the outset, with further products offering upside as eligibility is clarified.
•
Balance sheet repaired, with further funding likely in FY28E
– Placements of 67m shares at SGD0.10 (31 Oct 2025) and 75.8m shares at SGD0.198 (24 Feb 2026), together with warrant exercises, lifted cash and cash equivalents to SGD14.7m at 30 Jun 2026 from SGD0.9m a year earlier, and net assets to SGD15.4m from SGD0.4m.
The share count rose to about 1.07b in FY26 from 888m over the year.
We forecast operating cash outflow of SGD12.0m in FY27E as working capital builds ahead of DoD and compounding revenue, so cash is likely to fall to about SGD5.0m by end-FY27E.
We assume the shortfall is bridged by short-term borrowings, which could potentially rise to SGD18.4m by end-FY28E.
With Phase 3 externally funded, any further funding need is likely to be driven by Ligo Pharma and corporate overheads rather than by Wafermine.

title: If You Have S$10,000 to Invest, Should You Buy an ETF or Singapore Stocks?
article:
Deciding where to put your S$10,000, especially if it’s your first investment, can be terrifying.
Many investors choose between investing in individual stocks, which have greater potential to outperform the market, and
exchange-traded funds (ETFs)
, which offer instant diversification.
Both approaches have their advantages, so let’s look at which suits your needs better.
Option #1: Invest S$10,000 in an ETF
ETFs are baskets of stocks that track specific market indices or themes.
For example,
Vanguard Total World Stock ETF
(NYSE: VT) is a globally diversified ETF that holds almost 10,000 stocks.
For a more local approach,
SPDR Straits Times Index ETF
(SGX: ES3) tracks the
Straits Times Index
(SGX: ^STI) and contains 30 holdings.
ETFs lower the research burden because they simply hold whatever stocks are in the index they track and need little upkeep from you.
Investors should, however, watch out for fees and expense ratios, along with exchange rate fluctuation risks if they are investing in overseas ETFs.
Additionally, watch out for concentration risk.
The three local banks make up about 58% of the STI, so ES3 is heavily tied to the banking sector.
Related articles:
Can You Build an AI Portfolio Entirely with ETFs?
How to Invest in US Stocks from Singapore (Step-by-Step Guide)
Option #2: Build Your Own Portfolio of Singapore Stocks
Investors can tailor a portfolio of dividend-paying and/or growth companies to their income needs.
Blue chips such as Singapore’s largest bank,
DBS Group Holdings Ltd
(SGX: D05), with a 3.9% dividend yield, and telco giant
Singapore Telecommunications Limited
(SGX: Z74), or Singtel, at a 4.4% yield, can provide steady income.
Not only do investors stand to earn dividends, but they also stand to earn capital appreciation with individual stocks.
DBS’s share price, for example, rose 160% over the past five years, with shares trading at S$74.44 on 26 October 2026, up from S$28.67 on 25 October 2021.
Investing in individual stocks carries greater company-specific risk than a broadly diversified ETF.
It involves more active participation from investors, as they need to monitor individual companies’ financial results, valuations, and business developments.
S$10,000 also might not buy you enough shares to have a diversified portfolio in individual stocks.
Related articles:
Gotta Catch ‘Em All: A Guide to Building a Diverse Dividend Portfolio
Blue-Chip Stocks: The Safe, Steady Investments Every Beginner Should Know
ETF vs Singapore Stocks: Which Offers Better Returns?
Both Singapore’s blue-chip equities and the STI have delivered strong performances over the past five and ten years.

The comparison isn’t exact: the ETF’s returns assume dividends are reinvested, while the share price figures exclude dividends.
The ETF still pays out its dividends twice a year, and while its yield is lower than Singtel’s, it delivered far higher returns over 10 years.
It isn’t always clear-cut whether ETFs or individual stocks offer better returns, as many factors, including investment horizon and income needs, come into play.
Singapore dividend stocks, however, provide regular dividend payments, creating a potential source of passive income without requiring investors to sell their shares.
In contrast, a broad-market ETF tracking global or US equities can provide greater exposure to growth-oriented companies across sectors such as technology and healthcare that do not have a local equivalent.
Ultimately, the more suitable investment depends on whether an investor prioritises regular income, long-term capital growth or a balance of both, alongside their risk tolerance and investment horizon.

combines diversification from an ETF with the flexibility to select individual Singapore stocks.
Investors can consider:
70% (S$7,000) in a diversified ETF
30% (S$3,000) in selected Singapore stocks
The ETF forms the portfolio’s diversified foundation, and individual stocks provide opportunities to outperform the market and generate dividend income.
Which Approach Would I Choose with S$10,000?
An ETF with diversified exposure and low fees is an excellent investment for a novice.
Since the index decides what the ETF holds, you don’t need to research individual companies.
For those investing for income, Singapore dividend stocks are a good source of regular cash distributions.
Instead of simply focusing on yield, pay attention to whether the dividend is sustainable and supported by the company’s free cash flow.
Individual stocks are perfect for those investors who like to analyse companies and potentially earn more than the market.
Instead of choosing either ETFs or individual stocks, some investors may consider using ETFs as a base with additional individual stocks.
This choice offers a balance between
diversification
and the potential to outperform.
Get Smart: Start with the Strategy, Not the Stock
S$10,000 is enough to build a long-term investment portfolio.
ETFs offer diversification, simplicity, and a convenient way to invest.
Individual Singapore stocks provide dividend income and opportunities to outperform, but require more research and carry greater risk.
For me, a mixed 50/50 portfolio is preferred as it balances diversification from ETFs with the potential to outperform the market with individual stocks.
For conservative investors, ETFs can take a bigger portion of the pie.
Remember, building wealth ultimately depends more on investing consistently, managing risks, and allowing compounding to work over time.

title: Asian stocks to gain as Anthropic files for IPO
article:
(Oct 27) : Asian stocks were set to rise, tracking gains on Wall Street as Anthropic PBC’s initial public offering filing revived enthusiasm for artificial intelligence ahead of big tech earnings and the Federal Reserve’s rate decision.

Equity-index futures for Japan and South Korea pointed higher, while those for Australia were little changed. US stock contracts edged up in early Asian trading after the S&P 500 gained 0.7% and the Nasdaq 100 rose 1.1%. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index jumped 2.8%, its biggest gain since Sept. 21.

Brazilian markets tumbled after President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva won re-election, fueling concerns that fiscal strains in Latin America’s largest economy will worsen.

US oil declined after Brent settled below US$116 a barrel Monday as senior officials from several countries traveled to Tehran in a bid to revive talks aimed at preventing a broader escalation in the Middle East. Short-dated Treasuries slipped, the dollar edged higher and Bitcoin traded below US$80,000.

Anthropic filed its long-awaited S-1, moving closer to becoming the first publicly traded company focused primarily on developing advanced AI models. Investors are scrutinizing the filing for clues on AI demand after weeks of doubts over the trade. The offering will be a key test of appetite for the technology after AI enthusiasm helped power a four-year bull market in stocks.

The company “has clearly rekindled the sort of enthusiasm for all things AI-related that had been missing from the market’s zeitgeist for the past few weeks,” said Steve Sosnick at Interactive Brokers. “This IPO will be an important test of the market’s attitudes and appetites.”

See also: Oil declines as diplomacy offers hope of Mideast deescalation

The renewed optimism follows a volatile week for technology shares. The Nasdaq 100 tumbled 2.9% on Thursday, a day after Meta Platforms Inc. raised its capital-spending guidance above operating cash flow, rattling investors seeking evidence that massive AI outlays are paying off.

That question will be tested again this week when some of the biggest AI spenders report earnings. Alphabet Inc. and Microsoft Corp. are due Wednesday, followed by Amazon.com Inc. and Intel Corp. on Thursday. Investors will be watching their spending plans and, crucially, whether those investments are generating sufficient returns.

“The big focus is what these companies expect to spend on AI going forward and whether this spending can continue to be financed by cash flows, or if equity and debt issuance will be necessary,” said Richard Saperstein at Treasury Partners.

See also: Stocks get tech boost as Anthropic files for IPO

The Fed provides another major test Wednesday, with policymakers widely expected to leave rates unchanged after raising them in September. Chairman Kevin Warsh will need to reinforce the central bank’s commitment to containing inflation while explaining why officials opted against another increase.

Markets are pricing about a 10% chance of a hike Wednesday, compared with more than 70% odds of an increase by year-end.

“With so many firms reporting this week, we would typically say that macro factors will take a back seat to idiosyncratic results. However, we have the Fed on Wednesday and what could be a very tricky, complicated press conference,” wrote Christopher Harvey, head of equity and portfolio strategy at CIBC, in a note.

title: Oil declines as diplomacy offers hope of Mideast deescalation
article:
(Oct 27) : Oil fell for a second day as stepped-up diplomatic efforts bolstered hopes a broader escalation in the US-Iran war may be averted.

West Texas Intermediate dropped toward US$101 a barrel after losing 1.5% in the previous session, while Brent settled below US$116. Senior officials from Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey traveled to Tehran for discussions on Monday, with participants agreeing to continue talks, according to the IRIB news agency.

Elsewhere on Tuesday, Russian President Vladimir Putin will meet with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, as well as Qatar’s Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani, on the sidelines of an energy summit in Moscow.

Still, risks remain elevated across the region. The Saudi-led coalition said it destroyed three drones in Riyadh. In Lebanon, Hezbollah is preparing for a new regional war after receiving funds from Iran, Reuters said, citing security personnel. That followed clashes involving Yemen-based Houthi rebels.

Global crude benchmark Brent has surged by almost 90% this year, as the US-Iran war disrupted energy flows and drew Yemen’s Houthi rebels into the conflict, with repeated attacks on Saudi Arabia. Investors are bracing for a packed stretch of potential market catalysts, with Israeli elections on Tuesday, a Federal Reserve decision later this week, and the US midterms on Nov. 3.

In the Israeli contest, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is pledging to topple Tehran’s regime, with US President Donald Trump’s backing. His challenger, opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot, says Iran’s nuclear program must be stopped, but he’s added that regime change is “not an achievable goal.”

See also: Stocks get tech boost as Anthropic files for IPO

The Fed will deliver its policy decision on Wednesday, after tightening last month for the first time since 2023 to tackle still-too-hot inflation. In the run-up, Fed officials suggested they were in no hurry to raise interest rates again, despite gains in energy costs.

title: Stocks get tech boost as Anthropic files for IPO
article:
(Oct 27) : A revival of the artificial-intelligence trade fueled gains in stocks as Anthropic PBC filed for an IPO, with investors bracing for this week’s results from tech giants and the Federal Reserve decision.

The S&P 500 halted back-to-back losses. High-profile chipmakers rallied, sending a closely watched industry gauge up 2.8%. The Nasdaq 100 rose 1.1%. In a volatile session, Brent crude settled near US$116. Brazilian markets tumbled as President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva was re-elected, fueling fears that fiscal issues in Latin America’s largest economy will worsen.

Anthropic’s initial public offering will be a key test of AI sentiment after optimism surrounding the technology helped power a four-year bull market in stocks. The company behind Claude expects to begin trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the symbol ANT, a filing showed.

“ANT has clearly rekindled the sort of enthusiasm for all things AI-related that had been missing from the market’s zeitgeist for the past few weeks,” said Steve Sosnick at Interactive Brokers. “This IPO will be an important test of the market’s attitudes and appetites.”

Major AI spenders Alphabet Inc., Microsoft Corp. and Amazon.com Inc. are expected to show healthy growth when they report earnings this week. Wall Street will be interested in comments on how much they plan to spend on AI and the degree to which those investments are proving to be profitable.

“The big focus is what these companies expect to spend on AI going forward and whether this spending can continue to be financed by cash flows, or if equity and debt issuance will be necessary,” said Richard Saperstein at Treasury Partners.

See also: Oil holds biggest gain in week as Saudi attacks fan supply risks

Meantime, Kevin Warsh will face a familiar challenge if the Fed holds rates steady: He must reassure investors the central bank is committed to quashing inflation while explaining why officials chose not to raise rates.

“We don’t expect a Fed rate hike on Wednesday, as the bond market has already tightened credit conditions since the Fed’s last meeting,” said Saperstein. “We expect to hear tough talk on the inflation front combined with soft action.”

With policymakers responding primarily to energy-driven inflation pressures and currency dynamics rather than a materially overheating economy, this is likely to be a relatively shallow tightening cycle, according to Seema Shah at Principal Asset Management.

See also: Asian stocks to slide on tech rout, bonds rally

The Fed is likely to deliver a hike in December and another one in 2027, she added.

title: Mercuria says rival fears drove disputed Baltic tanker rate
article:
(Oct 27): Commodity trader Mercuria Energy Group accused the Baltic Exchange of continuing to publish the world’s benchmark oil tanker rate, despite distortions caused by the Iran war, because it feared losing business to a competitor.

Lawyers for Mercuria kicked off a London trial claiming that the Baltic Exchange should have suspended the benchmark rate after exports through the Strait of Hormuz were strangled by the conflict between the US, Israel and Iran. The Baltic Exchange said the commodity trader’s claim reflects “instability and opportunism”.

Founded in 1774, the Baltic Exchange plays a central role in setting global shipping rates. It maintains it was still possible to put a price on the freight risk, and that it had consulted consistently with the market after the Iran war severely disrupted oil shipments through Hormuz. Flows have since recovered close to pre-war levels.

In an April 14 call, a senior freight assessor described the risk of the benchmark being replaced by a competitor as “the overriding fear of what we do here”, according to a document given to the court by Mercuria’s lawyers before the hearing on Monday.

Mercuria also gave examples of tanker market participants, including the Baltic Exchange’s own staff, who called into question the continued publication of a rate for the route.

The trading house said that the Baltic Exchange’s freight assessor didn’t submit a value into the company’s internal system that’s supposed to represent his personal view of where the index will be. When he did eventually submit a value, it included comments such as “doesn’t make any sense to shed an opinion on this route — crazy that we have to!”

See also: Stocks under pressure before earnings, oil dips

The case calls into question a pricing tool that until the Iran war acted as the benchmark for oil tanker earnings across the globe. The key TD3C rate underpins contracts between tanker owners and their customers as well as billions of dollars in derivatives. It’s based on the cost of hiring a supertanker from Saudi Arabia’s Ras Tanura, inside the Persian Gulf, to China, and also serves as a reference point for other routes.

The Baltic Exchange is confident that it has met all its statutory, contractual and regulatory obligations in the production of the TD3C benchmark, Chief executive officer Mark Jackson said in a statement. The claim from Mercuria is “without merit,” he added.

Mercuria has “huge index-linked exposures, which it has failed to risk manage,” lawyers for the Baltic Exchange said. After being caught out by the sharp rises in the benchmark, Mercuria “wishes to unseat TD3C, and it is reaching for any available argument to do so,” they added.

See also: Swiss stocks becoming a haven from AI fears roiling markets

Mercuria’s lawyers said the evidence showed the Baltic Exchange did not suspend the index because it wanted to keep the market for certain freight agreements active, and to avoid the risk of being replaced by a rival.

One of the brokers who contribute to the index said on April 2 that it was “utter nonsense” to provide an assessment of the TD3C benchmark, given the unprecedented levels of disruption to traffic through Hormuz, according to another transcript presented by Mercuria.

Mercuria is urging the court to declare that the Baltic Exchange breached its obligations and ought to have suspended the TD3C route.

Lawyers for the Baltic Exchange said the risk of being replaced by a rival provider did not drive its decision making. The lawyers said passage through Hormuz was still possible.

“The Baltic’s decision to continue publishing TD3C, was a decision which was not taken lightly,” lawyers for exchange said in a court document countering Mercuria’s allegations.

The Iran war threw global commodity markets into turmoil by slashing shipments through Hormuz, which Tehran declared closed in the early days of the conflict. In recent months, volumes have recovered, with most trackers seeing shipments close to pre-war levels.

A spokesperson for Mercuria didn’t immediately respond to an email for comment.

Mercuria initially said it had incurred losses estimated to be in the hundreds of millions of US dollars as a result of the Baltic Exchange continuing to publish the index, but removed any estimate of financial losses from its most recent claim.
